title: Rick Explains Binary Search Like a Boss #CompetitiveProgramming
caption: Ever wonder how to search faster than linear? Rick breaks down binary search in 60 seconds! 🚀 #Algorithms

scenes.script: Alright, Morty, let me tell you about the coolest way to find stuff in a sorted list—binary search!
scenes.web_image: a person looking at a sorted bookshelf

scenes.script: Uh, Rick? Why not just look at each item one by one like a normal person?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png
scenes.web_image: a person searching through an unsorted pile of papers

scenes.script: Because that’s for losers, Morty! Binary search halves the list every time. Start with two pointers, L and R.
scenes.web_image: two arrows pointing at a sorted array

scenes.script: Okay, but how does that actually work? It sounds complicated.
scenes.web_image: a flowchart diagram of a binary search process

scenes.script: Simple! Find the middle element, compare it to what you’re looking for. If your target’s lower, go left; if higher, go right.
scenes.web_image: a split decision diagram with left and right arrows

scenes.script: Hmm, like when you’re trying to find a book on a shelf? You start in the middle and then narrow it down?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png
scenes.web_image: a person opening a book in the middle of a bookshelf

scenes.script: Exactly! And since you’re halving the list each time, it’s O(log n) — way faster than linear search.
Wait, so how do you handle the pointers? Like, where do they start?
scenes.web_image: two arrows at opposite ends of an array

scenes.script: Set L to -1 and R to the size of the array. Easy peasy, Morty!
scenes.web_image: a diagram showing initial bounds for binary search

scenes.script: Got it! But what about integer overflow? That sounds scary.
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty super angry biting his lips and frowning.png
scenes.web_image: a calculator showing an overflow error

scenes.script: Smart Morty! Use m = l + (r - l) / 2 instead of (l + r) / 2. No more overflow!
scenes.web_image: a code snippet demonstrating safe midpoint calculation

scenes.script: Okay, but what if the target isn’t in the array? Or there are duplicates?
scenes.web_image: an array with missing or duplicate elements

scenes.script: Then you either return -1 or adjust the bounds. Edge cases, Morty—deal with them!
scenes.web_image: a flowchart showing edge case handling

scenes.script: So binary search isn’t just for arrays? What else can it do?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty evil with a serious looking and a portal gun.png
scenes.web_image: a graph of a monotonic function

scenes.script: It’s like your portal gun, Morty! Works on any sorted or monotonic thing—finding roots, bounds, you name it.
scenes.web_image: a person using a tool to measure and find boundaries

scenes.script: Wow! So binary search is basically life’s cheat code?
scenes.web_image: a cheat code screen from a video game

scenes.script: Exactly, Morty! Now go practice before I make you use linear search forever!
scenes.web_image: a person practicing coding on a computer

topic: How do you implement a binary search algorithm?
